Examples

Claimball — local prediction and shared-ball presentation

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Ball presentation claims

Run Claimball to compare local avatar prediction with prediction of the whole world. These three soccer examples use different authority and display policies:

example model the ball
slopball co-op, peer-authoritative owned by the last toucher (play.Puppet)
speedball predict-world (echo_inputs) every avatar echoed; one predicted timeline
claimball predict-self + the claim only your avatar predicted; the ball predicted and claimed

Claimball keeps the ball @(gd_tick = "contested"), so each peer predicts the ball locally before the authority settles its state. A kicker uses plain @(gd_tick) (predict-self, echo_inputs = false): each peer predicts its own kicker and displays remote kickers from authority history with an interpolation delay. The game does not echo held input for remote prediction. A claim chooses how to display the ball as it moves between these timelines; it does not transfer gameplay authority.

Ball presentation claims#

A contested ball runs on the local predicted timeline while a remote kicker is drawn from delayed authority history. Drawing every ball pose from local prediction would show a remote shot before the remote avatar visibly kicks it. The ball's presentation—the displayed state and effects—therefore uses a claim weight. The live world pass claims the ball while the local kicker is in reach or the ball is still moving fast from that kicker's shot.

Odin
// claimball.odin world pass: update presentation claims only in the live pass.
if ksim.lane_live(&g.lane) {
	if my_kicker_in_reach || ball_still_fast_from_my_kick {
		ksim.lane_claim(&g.lane, ball.net_id)   // display the local predicted pose
	}
}

Claimed, the ball draws from your prediction. Unclaimed, it draws from the watched authority history, so an opponent's touch moves it beside their delayed avatar. lane_claimed reads the weight back (near 1 while claiming, decaying to 0 over ~¼s after).

Keep the claim while the ball continues moving quickly because of the local kick, even after it moves far from the player. Releasing based only on distance blends toward the watched view, which trails the predicted pose by the timeline delay. That blend can pull the displayed ball backward during its flight. Release when the ball slows so the poses converge before returning to the watched view; see util.odin's RELEASE_SPEED.

The goal reset is predicted: each screen snaps the ball home when its simulation crosses the line. The score changes only on the authority in ball_tick_then and replicates through the delta lane, Kit's field-change replication path.

Shell
bash build/build_scripts.sh examples/claimball
$GODOT --path examples/claimball                  # host, join from a second window
CLB_LATENCY=120 $GODOT --path examples/claimball  # compare local touches at 240ms RTT

bash examples/claimball/run.sh          # solo gate (CLAIMBALL_SINGLE_OK)
bash examples/claimball/native_run.sh   # claim-mode integration test, three peers (CLAIMBALL_NATIVE_OK):
                                        # a striker drives + claims the ball to a goal (claim near 1),
                                        # an idle watcher sees the same ball watched (claim 0)

WASD move · Space kick (aim with your movement) · Tab scores · Enter chat. Env: CLB_ROLE (host/join/single/serve) · CLB_PORT · CLB_NAME · CLB_TOKEN · CLB_LATENCY · CLB_BOT (striker/idle) · CLB_GOALS.

See docs/onboarding/07-the-competitive-turn.md for the walkthrough and docs/kit/sim.md for the full lane.
